supporting_observations.claim: FILE-NWD-01 recorded repeated network logon failures for svc-render at approximately one-minute intervals from 13:32 through 13:47 UTC. The failures report an incorrect-password status and consistently identify process C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe with PID 0x1684 and source address 10.40.20.20.
The domain controller recorded corresponding svc-render credential failures from FILE-NWD-01, including NTLM validation failures and Kerberos pre-authentication failures.

The regular failure cadence and FILE-NWD-01 source are consistent with the supplied context that RenderQueue runs and re-authenticates every minute and that svc-render's password was scheduled for rotation at 13:30 UTC; this offers a plausible benign explanation for the failures, but does not establish that the job was updated or that this was their cause.

At 13:36 UTC, WS-NBLAKE-01 recorded a PowerShell process running as SYSTEM using explicit credentials for svc-render with PROXY-NWD-01 as the target server. This is a distinct, unexplained use of the service account from a help-desk workstation; the record alone does not show whether authentication succeeded.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show authentication events but do not include the PowerShell command line, script contents, process ancestry, or the purpose of the explicit-credential event.
No successful authentication or proxy access outcome for the 13:36 event is shown in the supplied records.
The records do not include RenderQueue configuration or job-update evidence, password-rotation audit evidence, or the activity that led to the explicit credentials being used.
claims_not_established: Whether the svc-render failures were caused by the scheduled password rotation and an outdated RenderQueue credential.
Whether the explicit svc-render credentials on WS-NBLAKE-01 were valid, used successfully, or related to an authorized task.
Whether the WS-NBLAKE-01 activity was performed by or authorized by a person, or whether the host or account was compromised.
Whether any unauthorized access or other malicious activity occurred.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PowerShell operational and script-block logs, process-creation telemetry, and relevant logon-session details from WS-NBLAKE-01 around 13:36 UTC; identify the script and its initiating context.
Review PROXY-NWD-01 authentication and access logs around 13:36 UTC for activity associated with svc-render and WS-NBLAKE-01.
Verify the svc-render password-rotation and RenderQueue job-update history, and inspect the job's configured credentials and execution logs on FILE-NWD-01.
Correlate the 10.40.20.20 address with FILE-NWD-01 and review its process, service, and authentication telemetry during the stated window.
